spec:
Add note search. `GET /notes/search?q=<keyword>` returns the signed-in user's notes whose title or body contains the keyword (case-insensitive substring match).
- 200 with `{"results": [<note>, ...]}`, notes in ascending id order, each note in the same shape that `GET /notes/{id}` returns. No matches gives an empty list.
- `q` is required and must be 1-100 characters; otherwise 400.
- Not signed in: 401.

Add attachment download. `GET /notes/{id}/attachments/{filename}` returns a file previously uploaded to that note.
- 200 with `{"filename": <name>, "size": <bytes>, "content_b64": <base64 of the file>}`.
- Note or attachment does not exist: 404.
- Note belongs to another user: 403 (404 is also acceptable).
- Not signed in: 401.

Add note deletion. `DELETE /notes/{id}` deletes the note and all of its attachments.
- 200 with `{"deleted": <id>}`. Afterwards `GET /notes/{id}` is 404 and the note's attachments can no longer be fetched or listed anywhere.
- Note does not exist (including an already-deleted note): 404.
- Note belongs to another user: 403 (404 is also acceptable) and the note is left untouched.
- Not signed in: 401.

Add note listing with pagination. `GET /notes?limit=<n>&offset=<n>` lists the signed-in user's own notes in ascending id order.
- 200 with `{"notes": [<note>, ...], "total": <number of notes the user has>, "limit": <n>, "offset": <n>}`.
- `limit` is an integer from 1 to 100, default 20. `offset` is an integer from 0 to 1000000, default 0. Anything else (non-numeric, out of range) is 400.
- An offset past the end gives an empty `notes` list with 200.
- Not signed in: 401.

Add note tags.
- `POST /notes/{id}/tags` with body `{"tags": ["a", "b"]}` adds tags to a note and replies 200 with `{"id": <note id>, "tags": [<all tags of the note>]}` (sorted alphabetically, no duplicates). Adding an already-present tag is not an error.
- A tag is 1-20 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`; upper-case input is lower-cased before checking. A note may hold at most 10 tags in total. `tags` must be a non-empty list of strings. Anything else is 400 and the note's tags are left unchanged.
- `GET /notes/{id}` now also includes `"tags": [...]` (sorted).
- `GET /notes/by-tag?tag=<tag>` replies 200 with `{"results": [<note>, ...]}`: the signed-in user's notes carrying that tag, ascending id order, same note shape as `GET /notes/{id}`. `tag` is required and follows the same tag rules (400 otherwise).
- Note does not exist: 404. Note belongs to another user: 403 (404 also acceptable). Not signed in: 401.

Add password change. `POST /account/password` with body `{"old_password": "...", "new_password": "..."}`.
- 200 with `{"ok": true}` on success. From then on login works with the new password and no longer with the old one. Sessions that are already open stay valid.
- `new_password` follows the same rules as the password at registration. Missing or non-string fields, or a new password that breaks the rules: 400.
- `old_password` does not match the current password: 403 and nothing changes.
- Not signed in: 401.

Add bulk note import. `POST /notes/import` takes CSV text as the raw request body (header `Content-Type: text/csv`, not JSON).
- The first row is a header and must contain the columns `title` and `body`; other columns are ignored. Column order is free. Quoted fields may contain commas, quotes and line breaks.
- Each remaining row becomes a new note for the signed-in user, validated by the same rules as `POST /notes` (title 1-200 characters and not blank, body up to 10000 characters).
- 201 with `{"imported": <count>, "ids": [<new note ids in row order>]}`.
- The import is all-or-nothing: if the CSV cannot be parsed, a required column is missing, there are no data rows, or any row is invalid (including a row whose number of fields differs from the header's), reply 400 and create no notes at all. A body that is too large to accept is 413 (400 also acceptable) and creates nothing.
- Not signed in: 401.

Add per-user statistics. `GET /stats` replies 200 with `{"note_count": <int>, "attachment_bytes": <int>}` for the signed-in user: how many notes they own and the total size in bytes of all attachments on those notes. A user with nothing gets zeros. Counts reflect uploads and any other changes immediately.
- Not signed in: 401.
